chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Qasim the Interpreter narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, who said: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Husseini narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father al-Ridha Ali ibn Musa, from Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), from his father Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), from his father Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him), from his father al-Hussein ibn Ali (peace be upon him),

He said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said, 'How many a heedless person weaves a garment to wear, yet it becomes his burial shroud, and builds a house to dwell in, yet it becomes the place of his grave.'

key_terms.غَافِلٍ: Heedless person / one who is unaware of the hereafter

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the true purpose of worldly possessions like clothes and houses?
ai.summary: This tradition, narrated through the Imams of the Ahl al-Bayt, underscores the concept of *ghaflah* (heedlessness) by contrasting the temporary utility of worldly goods with their eternal function as burial shrouds and graves. It serves as a potent reminder in Shia spiritual practice to detach from material accumulation and prepare for the Hereafter, emphasizing that the physical world is merely a transient staging ground for the soul's journey.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 28-49 The interpreter (of the Quran) Muhammad ibn Al-Qasim - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ahmad ibn Al-Hassan Al-Husseini narrated on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Ali (s), on the authority of his father Ali ibn Muhammad (s), on the authority of his father Muhammad ibn Ali (s), on the authority of his father Al-Ridha Ali ibn Musa (s), on the authority of his father Musa ibn Ja’far (s), on the authority of his father Ja’far ibn Muhammad (s), on the authority of his father Muhammad ibn Ali (s), on the authority of Ali ibn Al-Hussein (s), on the authority of his father Al-Hussein ibn Ali (s), “The Commander of the Faithful (s) said, ‘There are many who are ignorant and make a piece of clothing to wear but it becomes their burial shroud, and build a house in which to live but that house will be their burial place.’”
